component.name: Garmin Companion
component.summary: Your Garmin data, read by a coach that remembers

description.p: Pulls your Garmin Connect history onto your own machine and answers questions about it, with an emphasis on where your heart rate actually spent the session — the thing Garmin's own app buries.

Everything is read from a local SQLite cache rather than from Garmin, so the screens open instantly and a question can't stall on a network hiccup mid-conversation. Sync is the only thing that talks to Garmin.

ul.li: Today — recovery numbers, the last session in full with its zone breakdown, and hard-effort drift across recent runs
Activities — the history, with per-lap splits and charts for one session
Health — resting heart rate, HRV, sleep, stress and body battery over time
Food — calories in against out, and hydration
Ask — questions answered by a model you choose, given only the metrics the question needs
Insights and Reports — correlations mined from the cache, each stating its sample size, and weekly summaries
Plan, Routes and Gear — saved workouts, routes grouped from GPS traces, and shoe and bike mileage

description.p: Garmin credentials live in your OS keyring, never in the database. The only data that leaves the machine is the metrics a question needs, and only when you ask one.

The daily nudge now arrives on a desktop at the hour you set it for, not whenever you next open the app. Turning it on keeps the app in the tray after you close the window, where it syncs on its own and works the nudge out from numbers taken minutes before it speaks.
It can start at login, into the tray, without a window. A desktop with no tray to sit in is detected rather than assumed, and there the app quits with its window as it always did.
Release notes shown after an update are rendered as text rather than as the characters used to write it, and Android shows them at all.

The app speaks first now. It checks the week against goals you set and raises the one thing worth raising, with the numbers behind it — most days that is nothing at all, which is deliberate. On Android the nudge arrives without opening the app.
Strength sessions get a screen: sets, reps, time under tension and how long you rested. The watch does not record what was on the bar, so there is no volume here and the screen says so.
A Fitness screen carries Garmin's own verdict — training status, the monthly load balance against the ranges it wants, race predictions and your records.
The app updates itself on Android now. It fetches the new version in the background and Android asks before replacing it — the first time, it will send you to allow installs from this app.
Android also wears the wallpaper's colours where the system offers them, draws to the edges of the screen, and answers the back gesture instead of closing.
Insights goes deeper: comparisons that control for effort, sessions paired against the morning after, and the shape of a training block rather than its size.
Android builds, and a phone layout to go with them — the navigation moves to a tab bar and sign-in opens in the system browser.
Linux packages now install a desktop entry and this metadata, so the app shows up properly in software centres. Windows ships an NSIS installer instead of an MSI.
Garmin credentials moved to the OS keyring, with an encrypted store on Android, which has none.
